mechanism_log: The system has a clear causal structure: Y3 is exclusively controlled by X1 and X3 in a multiplicative-like interaction (neither alone can push Y3 above 0.4 when the other is low). Y4 is exclusively driven by X2 (positive), X4 (positive), and X6 (negative). Y1 is driven by all six inputs — X4 most strongly, followed by X2, X5 (nonlinear threshold ~0.35-0.45), X6, X3, X1. Y2 is most reduced by X3 (strong), then X4, X1; and most increased by X6 then X2. The key tradeoffs are: (1) X6 helps Y1 but hurts Y2 and Y4; (2) X2 helps Y1 and Y4 but slightly hurts Y2. X1, X3, X4 are generally beneficial for most objectives. X5 has a threshold near X5≈0.35-0.45 for Y1 — below this Y1 is strongly negative (~-0.10), above it Y1 saturates at ~0.167. X5 has no effect on Y2, Y3, Y4.

The system has strong nonlinear (superadditive/multiplicative) interactions that my earlier linear model completely missed. When X1=X3=X4=1.0 simultaneously, all outputs scale dramatically beyond linear predictions. Key structure: Y3 is multiplicatively controlled by X1 and X3 only. Y4 is driven by X2 (positive), X4 (positive), X6 (negative), with superadditive gain when X2 and X4 are simultaneously high. Y1 is driven by all six inputs but with massive superadditive gain when X1,X2,X3,X4 are all simultaneously high (Y1 reached 1.039, 2.3× above previously observed max). Y2 shows a regime-dependent reversal: at midpoint inputs, X6 INCREASES Y2 (positive gradient), but at high-input regime (X1=X3=X4=1.0), X6 DECREASES Y2 (negative relationship). X5 has a nonlinear threshold for Y1 only (~0.35-0.45), with no effect on Y2/Y3/Y4. The true Y1/Y4 Pareto frontier is far richer than previously thought, achievable with X1=X3=X4=1.0 and varying X2 (0.2→1.0) and X6 (0.1→0.7).

new_findings: Y3 is ONLY driven by X1 and X3 — all other inputs (X2,X4,X5,X6) have zero effect on Y3 (gradient=0 confirmed)
Y3 has a multiplicative-like interaction: X1=0.1 yields Y3<0.4 regardless of X3 level (max Y3=0.201 at X3=1.0 with X1=0.1); similarly X3=0.1 yields Y3<0.4 regardless of X1 — need both above ~0.4
Y4 is ONLY driven by X2, X4 (positive), and X6 (negative) — X1, X3, X5 have zero effect on Y4
X5 shows a nonlinear threshold around X5≈0.35-0.45 for Y1: below plateau at -0.10, above plateau at +0.167; Y5 has zero effect on Y2/Y3/Y4
X6 creates a direct Y1 vs Y4 and Y1 vs Y2 tradeoff — increasing X6 raises Y1 (+0.308 gradient) but also raises Y2 (+0.160) and reduces Y4 (-0.070)
X1,X3,X4 are collectively beneficial: raising them increases Y1, decreases Y2 (X3 most), and satisfies Y3 constraint — no fundamental conflict among these objectives
The Y3 constraint requires X1≥~0.4 AND X3≥~0.4 simultaneously (at X1=0.4,X3=0.4: Y3=0.469, safely above 0.4)
surprises: X2 INCREASES Y2 (positive gradient +0.081) instead of decreasing it — I expected X2 to help minimize Y2 like other inputs do. This means maximizing Y1/Y4 via X2 comes at a cost to Y2.
X5 has zero effect on Y2, Y3, and Y4 — it only affects Y1 and only through a nonlinear threshold, not a smooth linear relationship. This makes X5 a pure Y1-booster with no tradeoffs.
Y3 is entirely decoupled from X2, X4, X5, X6 (zero gradient confirmed) — the constraint is much simpler than expected, requiring only X1 and X3 management.
X1=0.1 makes Y3=0.064-0.201 (always below 0.4) regardless of X3 level — the interaction is multiplicative-like, not additive, making the constraint combinatorially binding.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Move to OPTIMIZE phase. Key strategy: (1) Set X5 high (≥0.55) to capture Y1 plateau for free. (2) Set X1≥0.4 and X3≥0.5 to satisfy Y3 constraint while also helping Y1 and reducing Y2. (3) Set X4 high (helps Y1, Y4, reduces Y2 — no tradeoff). (4) Sweep X6 low-to-high at several X2 levels to map the Y1 vs Y2/Y4 Pareto frontier. (5) Test if X2 and X4 interact for Y1 or Y4. (6) Explore a few Pareto-optimal points trading off Y1 against Y2/Y4 via X2 and X6.

new_findings: Y1 can reach 1.039 at [1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.7] — 2.3× above the previously observed maximum of 0.450. The system has strong superadditive nonlinear interactions invisible at midpoint gradients.
Y2 minimum = 0.091 at [1.0,0.2,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.1] — beats previous best 0.1978 by 54%. The true Y2 floor is much lower than the linear model suggested.
Y4 maximum = 0.322 at [1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.1] — beats previous best 0.2100 by 53%.
In the high-input regime (X1=X3=X4=1.0), increasing X6 from 0.1→0.7 DECREASES Y2 (0.362→0.313) — the opposite of the midpoint gradient estimate (+0.160). This is a regime-dependent sign reversal.
All 6 new points are Pareto-non-dominated. HV improved from 0.1007 to 0.2436 (+142%) in a single round.
In the high-input regime, X2 effect on Y1 is ~1.0 per unit vs my midpoint estimate of 0.328 — ~3× stronger — confirming superadditive cross-input amplification.
Y3=0.997 is consistently achieved at X1=X3=1.0 across all new evaluations, confirming the multiplicative model.
surprises: Y1=1.039 completely breaks my linear model — I predicted 0.38 but got 0.948 at [1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.1], an error of +0.57. The OAT-based gradient sum badly underestimated superadditive interactions that only emerge when ALL inputs are simultaneously at high values.

X6 reverses its sign on Y2 in the high-input regime. My midpoint OAT said X6->Y2 gradient=+0.160, but at X1=X3=X4=1.0, X6 from 0.1 to 0.7 reduces Y2 from 0.362 to 0.313. This means the Y1 vs Y2 tradeoff via X6 almost vanishes at high input levels.
Y2 at [1.0,0.2,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.1]=0.091 is so much lower than expected (predicted 0.19) that the true minimum Y2 is well below what linear gradients suggested.
The best Y1 point [1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0,0.9,0.7] has Y2=0.313 which is only moderately high — the Y1-Y2 tradeoff is much less severe in the high-input regime than my model predicted.
My entire exploration strategy of OAT at midpoints fundamentally missed the regime that matters most. I should have tested extreme all-high combinations much earlier in the budget.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Budget exhausted. Final Pareto front has 7 non-dominated points with HV=0.2436. The key recommendation is to use X1=X3=X4=1.0 and X5≥0.5 as the baseline, then vary X2 (controls Y1/Y2/Y4 tradeoff) and X6 (controls Y1 vs Y4 tradeoff) to navigate the Pareto surface.
